title: Cervix anatomy: epithelium and transformation zone
description: The gynecology examination landmark: external os, canal, squamocolumnar junction and transformation zone in one close-up.

questions.question: What is the cervical transformation zone?
questions.answer: It is the region where squamous epithelium of the ectocervix and columnar epithelium of the endocervix meet and change over time.

questions.question: Why is the transformation zone important in cervical screening?
questions.answer: Many cervical precancerous changes arise near the squamocolumnar junction. Screening samples this region, but this atlas does not interpret individual test results.

questions.question: What is the ectocervix?
questions.answer: Part of cervix visible at the vaginal vault. Function: Covered by nonkeratinizing stratified squamous epithelium.

questions.question: Where is the endocervical columnar epithelium located?
questions.answer: Mucus-secreting simple columnar lining of the canal. Function: Produces cervical mucus under hormonal regulation.

questions.question: What is the function of the squamocolumnar junction?
questions.answer: Function: Migrates with age, hormones and pregnancy. Border where glandular and squamous epithelia meet.
